question: Which of the following drugs used in the treatment of female infertility is an analogue of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) capable of inhibiting gonadal steroidogenesis during continued treatment ?:
analysis: Buserelin is a GnRH analogue that, when used continuously, suppresses gonadotropin release, leading to decreased gonadal steroidogenesis. This makes it effective in controlling hormone levels in conditions like endometriosis and certain infertility treatments. Clomiphene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator, Cetrorelix is a GnRH antagonist, and Progesterone is a hormone, none of which function as a GnRH analogue with the described mechanism.
